basis: ASSUMED owned tailoring and folded-textile appearance, pre-registered 2026-10-14 before replacement measurement; not a published garment standard or photographic certification
measurement: All coordinates and lengths in metres. Local x is front-to-back along the rail, y spans garment shoulders, z is up. Torso and shoulder depth are 95th minus 5th percentile x over central 200 mm width, respectively 35–60 percent and 10–22 percent below highest skin point. Tailoring features carry bound face ranges; measure stand/fall height along z, placket/lapel width along y. Fold top relief is z range of top-cap vertices after removing best-fit plane; centroid drift is largest xy centre displacement of horizontal bands relative to bottom band. Minimum gap is actual rendered x bounds separation for hanging neighbours with overlapping y/z bands. Envelopes and 27 mm gap may not be enlarged. The 40/46 mm torso and 32 mm shoulder air depths are assumed compressed empty garments on wire hangers, not worn-body dimensions. Existing 0.8 mm fabric thickness remains unchanged. Fold offsets are bounded deterministic assumptions, not stochastic runtime entropy. Shoulder return curvature is maximum inward yz distance of an intermediate boundary section from its straight front/back chord; actual bound section vertices must occur in faces. Lapel and collar-point exterior offset is minimum face-centre x minus the front-panel x interpolated on actual yz-projected triangles wherever a front panel exists. These extra screens were registered after first-fix rejection and before revised geometry measurement. Before revised fold-edge measurement: edge contrast is front indentation minus back indentation in the middle height band (46–56 percent), relative to lower (32–43 percent) and upper (58–69 percent) bands. Front is minimum y, back maximum y. This distinguishes a front free-edge groove from a uniformly waisted pillow perimeter. Actual bound front-hem faces: z extent is return height, y extent is return depth, in metres. Separate solidified thin sheet turns over front lip and returns inward; rear folded edge remains continuous.
